title: 1952 AHSME Problem 23
statement: If \(\dfrac{x^2-bx}{ax-c}=\dfrac{m-1}{m+1}\) has roots which are numerically equal but of opposite signs, the value of \(m\) must be:

solutions.text:
Cross-multiplication gives \[ \begin{aligned} (m+1)x^2 &-(m+1)bx\\ &-(m-1)ax\\ &\quad{}+(m-1)c=0. \end{aligned} \] Roots that are equal in magnitude and opposite in sign have sum \(0,\) so the coefficient of \(x\) is \(0.\) Thus \[ m(a+b)+(b-a)=0, \] and \[ m=\frac{a-b}{a+b}. \]

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Clear the denominator and collect the equation as a quadratic in \(x\)
Opposite roots have sum zero, so the coefficient of \(x\) must vanish
